# Working Memory Stage — Vivify Future Vision

The vivify pipeline needs a RAM-resident analogical workspace where concept structures form and tension-test before earning filesystem persistence.

- The current pipeline commits directly: raw text → keywords → filesystem, with no intermediate stage where meaning can be fluid
- The working memory stage sits between inference and vivify commit — structures form, relate, and resolve in RAM before touching a file
- The filesystem receives the settled thought, not the arriving one; only stabilized structures cross the boundary

The tension score serves a different function in working memory than in the stored pipeline.

- In the current pipeline, tension measures left/right divergence after the fact
- In working memory, tension is the halting criterion: commit when it stabilizes, discard when it doesn't resolve
- High and changing tension = still intrusive, still arriving; stable tension = ready to persist

This maps to the logos model of intrusive thought — something that enters unbidden, carries meaning, and demands attention before consent.

- A modifier that acts without permission is intrusive in this sense: it enters the meaning-space before the thought has resolved
- The permission prompt is the consent mechanism the logos model requires
- Working memory is where intrusive thoughts are allowed to be intrusive before they earn the right to become files

The working memory stage connects directly to multi-model convergence.

- Intermediate embeddings from each model in the round-robin live in working memory, not on disk
- The co-occurrence graph stabilizes in RAM across iterations; only the stable graph commits
- Halting criterion is identical: tension stops changing = ready to persist

The reify/vivify duality points to this stage as the missing third term.

- vivify: raw text → structure (left to right)
- reify: structure → felt prose (right to left)
- working memory: the pre-vivify moment where meaning is still fluid, neither text nor structure, not yet a file
